title: FERRYMAN TAKES FAKES
description: A beat made only from one printed record: THE VELVET HEARSE, "Two Coins for the Ferryman" (1971, imaginary), slowed to 88 BPM in D minor, re-cut so the ferryman's chord comes early, with its own break, bass note, voice and bell. One reversed slice is derived offline.

tracks.description: The record as found, two bars straight, heard through the wall of the viewing room.
The counterfeit: head-a bar 1 cut into bar 4 on the and-of-three; later the same cut from the feral shout chorus; the two coins.
One 7/8 cycle of the crossing, retriggered every three and a half beats across 4/4.
Odile: the sung coins, a cry, the scat run, the long fall, the last breath.
The record's stop-time stabs and its unresolved last chord.
The viewing-room bell, two octaves down.
A reed bark, the steel string chirping like a toy laser, and the shout downbeat reversed.
Iggy's break kick (bar 2, beat 1) at its own speed, above the sub.
Iggy's break snare (bar 2, beat 2), laid back 20-28 ms.
Iggy's break snares with everything below 6.5 kHz taken away: the wires and the room, cut to a sixteenth.
The conga roll at the end of Iggy's break, one hand at a time.
The Deacon's one lone low F from the stop bar, played at every pitch of the bass line.
The shout downbeat reversed (bit-exact offline): it swells into the return.
